rows.evidence: Q1: Material & method / Tentative layout - a field experiment in Shiyan City (Hubei) during the 2011 cucumber season with three drip-irrigation treatments (reclaimed water, 50% reclaimed water, groundwater) in 4 m x 4 m plots, with soil NH4-N and NO3-N sampled at several depths on days 2, 5 and 9 after irrigation and NO3-N measured to 200 cm before and after the season (Figs. 1-3).
rows.notes: The study reports only soil nitrogen dynamics: NH4-N rises in topsoil after reclaimed-water drip irrigation and returns to pre-irrigation levels by day 9; NO3-N increases with depth (interpreted as a downward leaching tendency) and, under full reclaimed water, rises by 38.2%, 44.7%, 34.9% and 30.9% in the 0-50, 50-100, 100-150 and 150-200 cm layers over the season. No groundwater sampling or any measurement of nitrate reaching groundwater is reported; the conclusion that contaminants must enter the groundwater system is an assertion supported by citations [39,40], not by the study's own data. The study therefore supports only a precondition (residual/leaching nitrate in the soil profile) of the claimed harm to groundwater, so Q2 is no and upstream is set. Note also that the treatments contrast reclaimed water with groundwater under the same drip system, so the observed effect is attributable to the water source rather than to drip irrigation as such. No replication is described (one plot per treatment), no dispersion statistics are given, and no limitations beyond generic calls for further research are stated.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single-season, single-site, apparently unreplicated plot experiment; figures reproduced only as axis labels, so numerical values are taken from the text.
